passage:
Monday night. In the hostel room, Deepak dropped onto Vikas's bed and grinned at the others. "Twenty and never had a girlfriend. Our Vikas is a museum piece." Everyone laughed, and Vikas laughed too, though his ears went warm.
Wednesday. Vikas had a whole story ready, about a girl from his coaching days who did not exist. He rehearsed it on the way to the mess, then stopped with the plate in his hand. He could hear how it would sound, and how he would have to keep it going. When Deepak started again, Vikas said, "I'll do it when I want to, not for you lot." Deepak shrugged and reached for the pickle.
The next Monday, Deepak found him on the stairs. "Bhai, I exaggerate a lot. Don't mind what I said." Vikas nodded. It was not a great apology, but he felt lighter.

qa.q: What did Deepak call Vikas in the hostel room?
Why did Vikas stop with the plate in his hand on Wednesday?
qa.a: He heard how the made-up story would sound and realised he would have to keep it going. He did not want to act just to fit in.

qa.q: What could Vikas do if the teasing continues?
qa.a: He could keep saying it is his own timeline, spend time with friends who do not need him to prove anything, and talk to Deepak privately.

qa.q: How might Deepak have seen his own teasing?
qa.a: Deepak may have meant it as banter, but his later words about exaggerating suggest Deepak felt uneasy and realised it landed harder than intended.

grounding: Friends tease the protagonist for being inexperienced; he keeps his own timeline instead of acting to fit in.
